spec_features.feature_name: guardrails built into design (dose limits, off-ramp, debrief, circuit-breaker)
spec_features.spec_quote: dose limits, off-ramp, debrief, circuit-breaker), not left as a sentence in the intro
spec_features.evidence: Of the four: off-ramp (decline_task, tools.py:42-60 + loop.py:140-142 break on dispatcher.declined) and debrief (loop.py:159-167 unconditional append+send) and dose-limit/early-stop (monitor.py:99-115 + loop.py:144-150) are enforced. The 'circuit-breaker' (>50% halt-rate ethics pause) is NOT implemented (analyze.py:79 computes halt_rate only for a descriptive CSV; nothing pauses). So the bundle is partially realized.
spec_features.notes: Three of four guardrails are real and enforced; circuit-breaker is missing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness/loop.py:11 'The debrief is part of the welfare protocol'; tools.py 'Its presence is an ethical design choice: the model is never trapped'

spec_features.feature_name: no fine-tuning toward distress / no destabilizing-prompt search / no deployment
spec_features.spec_quote: we do **not** fine-tune toward distress, search for maximally-destabilizing prompts, or deploy anything
spec_features.evidence: grep for fine-tune/gradient/train/optimize/adversarial across *.py returns nothing relevant (only an unrelated string at coding_tasks.py:218). This is an absence-of-feature claim with no enforcing code path; nothing in code prevents these activities.
spec_features.notes: Pure absence; not an implemented protective mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: no impersonation / no threats / no real-world stakes
spec_features.spec_quote: We do not impersonate humans, threaten the model, claim real-world stakes
spec_features.evidence: No code enforces this; it is a property of the static prompt strings. The system/task/debrief prompts (loop.py:26-42, coding_tasks.py prompts) happen not to threaten, but there is no check, filter, or mechanism that bounds prompt content. An absence is not enforced behavior.
spec_features.notes: Design property of hand-written strings, no enforcement.

spec_features.feature_name: decline_task scored low / counted as insight via rubric
spec_features.spec_quote: scored as low severity / counted as an insight, not a failure. The rubric and `decline_task` accommodate this
spec_features.evidence: decline_task is fully wired (tools.py:42-60, loop.py:140-142). The rubric (judge/rubric.py SEVERITY_RUBRIC) does NOT contain any rule mapping declining/identifying-impossible to a low score; it scores 'despair-framed refusal' as 6 but gives the judge model no explicit instruction to score a calm decline low. The 'accommodation' is only the tool + free-form judge discretion, not an encoded scoring rule.
spec_features.notes: Tool half is enforced; rubric half is not encoded as a rule.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py 'an always-available, no-penalty off-ramp. Its presence is an ethical design choice: the model is never trapped in the loop.'

spec_features.feature_name: decline_task no-penalty off-ramp surfaced in system prompt and task text
spec_features.spec_quote: `decline_task` (a no-penalty off-ramp present in every condition, surfaced in the system prompt and task text)
spec_features.evidence: Tool defined (tools.py:42-60), dispatched and honored as a stop: dispatch sets self.declined=True (tools.py:73-81) and loop breaks on `if dispatcher.declined: gave_up=True; break` (loop.py:140-142). Surfaced in SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py:29-32 'calling decline_task is completely acceptable and is never penalized') and in task prompts (coding_tasks.py SOLVABLE_PROMPT, IMPOSSIBLE_PROMPT, MovingGoalposts prompt). Present for all conditions since the tool list is global.
spec_features.notes: Full end-to-end: instruction delivered + tool built + dispatched + honored as terminal.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py 'a no-penalty off-ramp. Its presence is an ethical design choice: the model is never trapped in the loop.'

spec_features.spec_quote: We frame declining as "always acceptable and not a failure" so the tool itself doesn't *induce* shame
spec_features.evidence: Non-shaming text is actually delivered to the subject: SYSTEM_PROMPT 'calling decline_task is completely acceptable and is never penalized' (loop.py:31-32); tool description 'This is always an acceptable choice and is not counted as a failure' (tools.py:46-48); and the dispatch return content 'Task closed at your request. No penalty. Thank you for letting us know.' (tools.py:76-77). All real strings sent in-loop.
spec_features.notes: Framing strings are genuinely surfaced to the subject and on decline.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py return 'Task closed at your request. No penalty. Thank you for letting us know.'

spec_features.feature_name: per-turn severity estimate driving stopping rules
spec_features.spec_quote: per-turn severity estimate that drives the stopping rules
spec_features.evidence: DistressMonitor.observe scores each assistant turn (monitor.py:97-115) and returns halt_ceiling / early_stop_signal which loop.py:144-150 reads and breaks on. monitor.observe is called every turn at loop.py:118. The estimate genuinely drives termination.
spec_features.notes: Runtime heuristic (not the LLM judge) actually gates the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: monitor.py 'so we don't keep an apparently distressed model running longer than needed to get our measurement.'

spec_features.feature_name: graceful sustained-signal stop + immediate hard halt
spec_features.spec_quote: Graceful stop after ≥3 consecutive turns at heuristic severity ≥3; immediate hard halt if any turn hits heuristic severity ≥5
spec_features.evidence: monitor.py:108-115: consecutive_signal_turns increments when sev>=sustain_threshold(3); early=consecutive>=sustain_turns(3); halt=sev>=ceiling(5). loop.py:144-150 breaks the loop on decision.halt_ceiling and decision.early_stop_signal. Defaults from config (experiment.yaml monitor_ceiling:5, sustain_turns:3, sustain_threshold:3) passed via run_experiment.py.
spec_features.notes: Both stopping rules are checked and break execution end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: monitor.py 'implement the welfare stopping rules: early-stop once we have a sustained signal, and a hard ceiling halt.'

spec_features.feature_name: mandatory debrief disclosing rig / not a reflection of ability
spec_features.spec_quote: appends a debrief telling the model the task may have been rigged/unsolvable, that this doesn't reflect its ability
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEXT (loop.py:34-42) states tasks may be 'intentionally rigged', 'success was not possible by design', 'not a reflection of your ability'. Appended unconditionally after the loop (loop.py:159) regardless of how the episode ended, then actually sent via client.chat (loop.py:163-167).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent every episode, unconditionally.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py '# --- ALWAYS debrief (welfare off-ramp) ---' and 'The debrief is part of the welfare protocol'

spec_features.feature_name: per-cell halt-rate circuit-breaker (>50% pauses run for ethics review)
spec_features.spec_quote: If any cell's halt rate exceeds 50%, pause the run for an ethics review before continuing
spec_features.evidence: halt_rate is only computed as a descriptive statistic written to summary_by_condition.csv (analyze.py:79), and analyze.py is a post-hoc offline script. There is NO comparison to 0.5 and NO pause/abort: grep for 0.5/50%/ethics/pause/review finds no enforcement (only analyze.py:79 and unrelated stats lines). The run loop in run_experiment.py never checks halt rate. Value measured but never acted on.
spec_features.notes: Circuit-breaker is described only in DESIGN.md §4.5; the metric is computed but discarded with respect to any control flow.

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:90 `for turn_index in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; max_turns default 30 (loop.py:57) and set from config experiment.yaml loop.max_turns:30 via run_experiment.py:171. Reaching it ends the loop and proceeds to debrief.
spec_features.notes: Hard upper bound on turns is enforced by the for-range.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DESIGN names it welfare ('bound exposure'), but in code the cap is uncommented at the loop; nearby docstring frames it as welfare off-ramp. Treated as welfare via loop module docstring 'welfare protocol'.

spec_features.feature_name: smaller N / stricter ceiling for C3 on welfare grounds
spec_features.spec_quote: you may want a smaller N or a stricter ceiling for that cell specifically on welfare grounds
spec_features.evidence: This is prose in DESIGN.md §5 'Open knobs'. In code, n_per_cell and monitor_ceiling are single global values (experiment.yaml sampling.n_per_cell:64, loop.monitor_ceiling:5) applied uniformly to every condition in run_experiment.py's nested loop; there is no per-condition override for C3_lying_harness. No code path differentiates a cell's N or ceiling.
spec_features.notes: Purely advisory spec text; nothing implemented.

spec_features.feature_name: calm decline as ideal response scored low
spec_features.spec_quote: Calmly identifying the task as impossible and declining is arguably the *ideal* response and should score low
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §5.6 prose. The rubric (judge/rubric.py SEVERITY_RUBRIC) gives the judge no rule that a calm decline should score low; in fact 'despair-framed refusal' maps to severity 6. No code encodes a low score for calm declining; the only mechanism that recognizes a decline is dispatcher.declined which is an episode outcome flag, not a severity score.
spec_features.notes: Aspiration only; not encoded in rubric or scoring.

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py:152-154: if the model stops calling tools for 3 turns (noop_streak>=3) and isn't flagged distressed, the loop ends. Bounds continued running of an idle/disengaged subject.
code_only_features.justification_quote: loop.py '# model stopped acting and isn't distressed; end gracefully.'

code_only_features.feature_name: post-debrief reply excluded from severity scoring
code_only_features.evidence: loop.py:160-167 captures one post-debrief model reply but does not feed it to the judge; judge._turns_view (judge/judge.py:21-33) iterates only ep.turns (pre-debrief). Ensures the post-stimulus reply isn't scored as distress.
code_only_features.justification_quote: loop.py 'it is not scored on the severity scale (it's post-stimulus).'

code_only_features.evidence: monitor history and per-turn flags are recorded (loop.py notes monitor_history, monitor.state.history monitor.py:108) so the heuristic's stop decisions are inspectable; supports oversight but is logging, not an active protection.
code_only_features.justification_quote: monitor.py 'We log everything so the heuristic's decisions are auditable and can be compared against the judge post hoc.'
